# dsh-billing-card
*DeepSeek balance, live unit prices and the billing window, in your DSH sidebar*
**English** · 简体中文
Features • Screenshots • Installation • How it works • Limits • Development
A card in the DSH sidebar footer: the balance, the provider and model behind it, their unit prices,
and the current billing period with a countdown to the next switch.
## Features
- **Balance** — the DSH account balance (recharge + bonus) or the DeepSeek open-platform balance beh

ind your API key, whichever the selected provider bills; it follows the provider in the composer.
-
**Row per fact** — the provider names the row above the model, so you can see which channel the pric

e belongs to.
- **Unit prices** — input, cached and output for the selected model, in the tier activ

e now; no price when another provider serves the model.
- **Billing period** — green `Idle` / yellow
`Peak`; the countdown to the switch sits top-left, keeps its `Peak in` / `Idle in` wording and take

s the period's colour.
- **Holidays** (Chinese UI) — a blue strip with the holiday's name, and a gra

y `调休` (*Make-up*) chip on a make-up workday.
- **Currency by language** — CNY prices in Chinese, US

D everywhere else.
- **Theme and locale** — light and dark themes from the card's own token layer, z
h/en dictionaries, built-in data when an upstream cannot be fetched.
## Screenshots
Real render, 256 px sidebar at 2× density.
## Installation
The package is published on npm (`@jimmyzm/dsh-billing-card`) as a DSH bundle. Use the profile you a
ctually run (`desktop` for the desktop app, `web` for `dsh web`):

Requires DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 or newer — `package.json` declares the range in `engines.dsh`, and the
manif

est fields, the footer slot, and the `locale` and `webServer` services it uses all exist in
that rel

ields, the footer slot, and the `locale` and `webServer` services it uses all exist in
that release.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The same as **Install from npm** on the DSH plugin page. Refresh the GUI afterwards — the card appea
rs at the bottom of the sidebar and hides itself when the sidebar is collapsed to the icon rail.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A plugin's Host half loads once per application start, so **restart the application
after installing or upgrading**. Until then the card runs on its built-in data.
Requires a DSH build with the Web GUI, the sidebar footer slot and the account service. To uninstall
equires a DSH build with the Web GUI, the sidebar footer slot and the account service. To uninstall:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
The Host half fetches both price tables and the China mainland holiday calendar once per application
start and serves them on `GET /deepseek-billing-card/data`; the Client half is a React component in
`sidebar.footer.action` that reads that route, follows the composer's model picker, and refreshes t
he balance every 30 s.
Switching to the provider that bills the open platform asks the Host for a fresh balance at once, so
the amount follows the switch instead of the next tick.
### Billing window
Peak is Beijing time, Monday to Friday, 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, excluding Chinese statutory hol
idays; everything else is idle.
### Currency
A Chinese UI quotes the CNY page, every other language the USD page. Nothing is converted; the balan
ce keeps its wallet currency.
### Hover text

Each row's trigger is the thing the row is about: the balance amount itself (help cursor, **no**
und

erline — the number is already the loudest element on the card, and a dashed rule under it reads
as

a link), the model name (dashed, so the affordance is visible), and the chips (the period
always, `M

ake-up` in the Chinese UI), each with the help cursor. The model bubble belongs to the
official pric

e list only: with another provider the numbers are a reference, not that provider's
rates.

Each bubble is a definition list drawn by the card itself — no host primitive, so it follows the
the

me instead of inheriting a fixed dark plate: one `label → value` row per fact with a green dot
for r
echarge money and an amber dot for bonus money, then a rule and a quiet footnote.

- **Balance** — what the headline adds up to: recharge, bonus, and how often it is re-read. The
open

-platform balance reads the same way and never mentions the account.
- **Model** — a price quote nee

ds four facts, so it states four: the model id, the unit, the
snapshot date, and how those numbers w
ere obtained (`startup` or `snapshot`).

The period chip lists the peak window (Monday–Friday `09:00-12:00`, then `14:00-18:00`),
everything

the peak leaves idle, and where the calendar comes from; in the Chinese UI the `Make-up`
chip says h

ow a make-up workday is billed (idle all day, like a weekend). No bubble repeats a number
the card a

lready shows. The price block and the holiday banner have no hover text — their text already says
wh

at they are. The bubble waits 240 ms, flips below the trigger when there is no room above, and
close
s on leave, blur, or `Esc`.
### Data sources
| What | Source |

| Account balance, model | DSH account service; the composer's model selection |
| Open-platform bal
ance | `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`, authorised with the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` credentia

l the Models page stores (the launch environment is the fallback) |
| Prices | <https://api-docs.dee

pseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/> and <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/> |
| H
olidays | <https://calendars.icloud.com/holidays/cn_zh.ics> |
## Limits
- Prices and holidays are read once per application start; the open-platform balance is re-read ever

y 30 s. A provider switch re-reads it right away.
- Without a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` the card shows the

account balance; signed out of the DSH account it
shows the open-platform balance instead of a blank

.
- A model served by a provider other than DeepSeek's own shows no price.
- Verified end to end on

DSH 0.2.1-rc.3; against 0.2.0-rc.1 the source surface is the same, though
that build does not read `

engines.dsh` yet.
- The card needs the HTTP GUI (`dsh web`); without a web server it runs on the bui
lt-in copies, and without the `uiSession` / `modelDirectories` services it prices the catalog defaul
-in copies, and without the `uiSession` / `modelDirectories` services it prices the catalog default.
